lede: The meeting that deserves your attention this week is TMVOA's July 31st board session, where proposed amendments to the organization's fiscal policies and procedures get 30 minutes of dedicated agenda time — the most of any item — alongside board officer elections and fall/winter programming decisions. Over in Ouray County, a virtual-only planning commission work session on August 5th is quietly doing the kind of foundational work that matters: reviewing possible changes to Land Use Code definitions, where a single word shift can reshape what the rules actually allow. The rest of the week's government calendars are largely blank — most agendas haven't posted yet.

notable.stake: Fiscal policy amendments and new board officer elections could reshape TMVOA governance.
Land use code definition changes can quietly rewrite what development rules actually permit.
